name: The Emperor
upright: Security steered from the top, aligned to business goals and written down from policy to procedure.
reversed: A ruler who delegates the blame: shelfware policies, security for its own sake and no one accountable.
vision: A ruler sits on a stone throne carved with two ram heads, wearing a crown that cannot be lifted off and handed to anyone else. The left ram studies a map of the realm; the right ram walks the road it shows. In one hand the ruler holds a golden orb that is really a compass, its needle fixed on the merchants' trade routes; the ankh scepter in the other hand swings wherever the needle points. Behind the throne, the barren mountains rise in five terraces: a single peak that speaks the law, ridges of exact rules, a level plateau no camp may sink below, meadows of optional signposts, and a staircase carved one step at a time.
decode: The crown that cannot be handed off → senior management holds ultimate accountability; tasks can be delegated, accountability cannot.
The ram reading the map, the ram walking the road → due diligence is knowing and planning what to do; due care is doing it, as a prudent person would.
The orb compass on the trade routes, the scepter that follows it → governance is top-down and aligned to business strategy, goals and mission.
Five terraces → policy (mandatory, high level), standards (mandatory specifics), baselines (minimum configurations), guidelines (optional), procedures (step by step).
facts: ISO/IEC 27001 sets the requirements for an ISMS and is certifiable; ISO/IEC 27002 is the supporting control guidance and is not certifiable.
A strategic plan looks about five years ahead, a tactical plan about one year, and operational plans are short term and highly detailed.
COBIT, from ISACA, governs enterprise IT; NIST CSF 2.0 groups outcomes into six functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover.
trap: The collective keeps writing products into policy. A policy states broad, mandatory intent and rarely changes; specific technologies belong in standards, and guidelines are the only optional layer.
